x: The time was slow, due mainly to the rough track, but conditions were the same for everybody and our man is to be congratulated on his good running. In the 880 yards Alby Bird met his "bogey man," A.

Robertson, the English International, chased Tom home, but he lost ground each lap at the water jump, which was a very stiff one. In the 880 yards Alby Bird easily qualified for the final, with MacCabe of the L.A.C., as also did A.

The holders of the trophy were the Thames Valley Harriers and after making a very bad start in the 100 yards scratch race, they more or less gave up heart and did not compete in the final event. They took this stand on the condition of the track, and A.

It was one of Pack’s best runs to date and if he could only find something of a finish, I would back him against the best in the country. In the 880 yards Alby Bird ran his usual consistent race and although coming up against his “bogey” man, A.
On 23rd/24th June 1933 A.G.White finished 3rd in the Brighton and Back with a time of 20hrs. 48mins. 16secs. Before the 1930's were over two more individual medals were won by Club walkers; by F.
